description: Six square waves through a bandpass and a highpass, played as a short closed hat and a long open hat, in the manner of the 808 hi-hat

params.text: Sets the base frequency of the six squares, 1000Hz to 2000Hz; each one runs at that plus a fixed offset of 100Hz, 250Hz, 400Hz, 550Hz, 600Hz or 1000Hz
Sets how fast the open hat fades, 50ms to 250ms; the closed hat is fixed at 10ms, and the tooltip and the manual say the top here is 300ms
With it on, a closed-hat trigger silences the open hat at once; with it off the two ring past each other, and a new module comes up off
Sets the centre of the bandpass filter the six squares pass through, 1000Hz to 5000Hz
Sets the corner of the highpass filter after the bandpass, 10000Hz fully anticlockwise down to 1000Hz fully clockwise, and drops the makeup gain from 10 to 2 as it turns
Plays the closed hat, and chokes the open hat when the choke switch is on; a rising edge at the closed-hat jack does it too
Plays the open hat; a rising edge at the open-hat jack does it too

inputs.text: A rising edge above 0.5V plays the closed hat; the length of the gate makes no difference
A rising edge above 0.5V plays the open hat; the length of the gate makes no difference

outputs.text: The closed hat, up to 5V peak
The open hat, up to 5V peak

notes: a CV input is bipolar and is added to its knob: 10V there is worth the knob's whole travel, -10V cancels a knob that is fully up, and the total is clamped to the knob's own range
both hats are cut from the same six oscillators through the same bandpass, so PITCH and BRIGHTNESS settings reach each of them
the manual says four square oscillators; there are six
